geometry_edits.rationale: Reduce the bend to preserve a cleaner dominant bar and avoid over-articulating the silhouette.
Simplify the executable path so the mass reads less like a segmented polygon and more like one continuous gesture.
Deepen the courtyard to improve void publicness and sectionally separate the active ground from the upper mass.
Keep the void opened to the verified access side so the frontage reads as an intentional threshold.

graph_edits.rationale: Open the court slightly more so the void reads as a meaningful public ground figure rather than a shallow incision.
Keep the court aligned to the verified access side so the frontage responds as a legible public threshold.
Bring the terrace link lower to strengthen the ground-response and make the access edge feel more occupied.

rationale: The candidate reads as a single bent bar with a carved court, so it has a recognizable dominant gesture and some hierarchy. The four views are broadly consistent, and the mass does not appear catastrophically self-colliding. However, the form is still somewhat generic and box-derived, with the carved void not yet becoming a clearly public ground response. For the neighborhood-living brief, the access edge does not resolve into a strong, legible street threshold; the void is present but only moderately public. Sectionally, the mass feels more like a manipulated prism than a genuinely program-specific live/work neighborhood body with a strong active ground and calm upper hierarchy. So it is promising but not a hard program fit yet.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Much taller tower logic than this neighborhood-living brief; useful only as a profile precedent, not as a typology.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Tall massing with a strong profile and stepped/tapered upper articulation can still read as one dominant figure when the base remains legible.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: More single-story and pavilion-like than the candidate; use only the ground-edge logic, not the scale.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A compact commercial mass can gain program clarity through a simple primary volume plus a distinct attached threshold/canopy element.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: This is a counterfactual larger residential precedent; it demonstrates sectional continuity and courtyard/public-space consequences more than exact form.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A continuous inhabitable section can organize a strong communal void/court while maintaining a coherent upper mass and terrace logic.

warnings: Visible access-edge response is under-articulated for the verified road frontage.
The void reads more as a subtraction than as a clearly occupied public court or entry seam.
Upper mass is coherent, but the section still feels closer to an abstract bent object than a program-driven neighborhood building.
